message.content:
At a pressure of **10 kPa** the freezing (melting) point of pure water is roughly **–2 °C**.  
This value comes from the water phase diagram: as the pressure falls below atmospheric levels, the solid‑liquid equilibrium line shifts downward, so the temperature at which ice melts (or water freezes) becomes colder. At 10 kPa the equilibrium lies just below –2 °C, giving the approximate freezing point you’re looking for.
